Medicare waste isn't theoretical—it's crushing patients right now. Orange County doctors are seeing it firsthand: bureaucrats burning through trillions while essential care gets squeezed.

H.R. 879 barely scratches the surface. We need real reform, not band-aids. When physicians can't serve patients because D.C. paper-pushers are burning cash on pet projects, that's not just waste—it's failure.

The solution? Cut the bloat, not the care. Track every dollar with blockchain verification. Make bureaucrats who sign off on wasteful spending personally accountable. Redirect funds from administrative overhead straight to frontline medicine.

Efficiency isn't optional when lives are at stake. For millions of patients counting on Medicare, it's the difference between getting care or getting left behind.

Section 102(b)(1)(D) rewards those who broke immigration laws with college access and work permits, while our veterans get put on waiting lists for healthcare. 

Real reform starts with ending catch-and-release, deporting criminal aliens, and making Mexico pay for the wall – not handing out privileges to those who jumped the line.

The research from Johns Hopkins on psychedelic therapies for PTSD is promising—especially for veterans who’ve been failed by decades of bureaucratic drug approval delays and Big Pharma’s stranglehold on mental health treatments. But let’s not ignore the elephant in the room: Why did it take until 2025 for D.C. to prioritize this?

The same government that greenlit $55 million for psychedelic studies at Hopkins also approved $1.7 trillion omnibus bills stuffed with foreign aid and non-defense pork. Veterans deserve cutting-edge care now, not after 20 years of FDA red tape.

Every dollar spent on real solutions like psilocybin therapy is a win, but the real scandal is how much taxpayer money gets wasted on outdated, ineffective programs while breakthroughs like this fight for scraps.
